subject: Ubuntu Packages Built for i386 and amd64 for Testing

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Ubuntu Packages Built for i386 and amd64 for Testing
parts:
Hi all,

After a few days of heads-down work, I've finally wrangled
launchpad.net to build rApache packages for i386 and amd64 on lucid.
The name of the package is libapreq2-mod-rstats, which follows the
debian naming convention for apache modules. I first thought to name
it libapreq2-mod-r, but that just didn't look right, so I borrowed the
rstats from the popular twitter hashtag.

If you're interested in testing please use the following sources.list
lines (I've placed these in
/etc/apt/sources.list.d/jeffreyhorner-ppa.list):

deb http://ppa.launchpad.net/jeffreyhorner/rapache/ubuntu lucid main
deb-src http://ppa.launchpad.net/jeffreyhorner/rapache/ubuntu lucid main

Be sure to add the gpg key for the launchpad PPA I created like so:

gpg --recv-keys 8BA137BC95566D14
gpg --export --armor 8BA137BC95566D14 | sudo apt-key add -

Cheers,

Jeff
--
http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/JeffreyHorner

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: Ubuntu Packages Built for i386 and amd64 for Testing
parts:
On Thu, Aug 26, 2010 at 12:37 PM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Very nice. Some questions:
> Does it automatically add the loadmodule line to the apache2.conf?

Yes it does. the post install script runs a2enmod automatically. And
when the package is removed, a2dismod is called.

> Do you think the binary compatible with both R 2.10 that is on the ubuntu
> repo, and the latest version from CRAN?

I'm a little unclear on the details of binary compatibility, but as I
understand as long as the R API has not changed, then it's okay.
However, I would recommend that you test first because the errors that
you encounter may be far stranger.

Can anyone else comment on binary compatibility?

Jeff
